dedupe_keys.name: a deep transfer learning powered edos detection mechanism for 5g and beyond network slicing

description: FortisEDoS incorporates the CG-GRU deep-learning model to detect traffic associated with denial-of-service behaviour in elastic 5G and beyond network slices. Graph and recurrent representations capture spatial and temporal relationships, while transfer learning adapts information from earlier slices to newly deployed ones. The paper reports experimental comparisons of detection and computation overhead. This is a source-established network-protection model; exact traffic data, training configuration and numerical effect sizes remain unavailable in the abstract. No operational attack instructions or packet contents were collected, and no deployed protection guarantee is inferred. The source authors provide the native description and file descriptors through Zenodo. The deposited documents or data declare CC BY 4.0 and public access. Geographic and temporal coverage remain bounded to explicitly named tests or locations, with other fields unknown. Only metadata was inspected, without reading measurements, archives, source code or document bodies. Related project reports may overlap; independent sample counts and equivalent test conditions are not assumed. This supports the source-defined communication system performance simulation role. Public paper access and licence do not establish executable availability, software rights or operating costs.
